topic: Back pain when bending to put on shoes and socks

slides.headline: Socks and shoes the hardest part?
slides.sub: Why bending forward can hurt, and some easier ways to get dressed.

slides.title: Why this movement catches
slides.body: Pulling on socks means bending forward, balancing and reaching all at once. When your back is irritable, that combination often feels worse than bending to pick something up.

slides.title: Sit down to dress
slides.body: Sit on the edge of the bed or a chair, then bring your foot up onto the opposite knee. This keeps your back more upright and takes the balance challenge away.

slides.title: Use the tools
slides.body: A long-handled shoehorn and slip-on shoes make flare-up days easier. Needing them for a while isn't a step backwards, it's a sensible way to keep moving.

slides.title: Train the movement back
slides.body: Gentle hip hinges, seated forward bends and knee-to-chest stretches, done little and often, usually help the movement feel easier. Most people improve as confidence and mobility return.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: Pain that spreads below the knee, numbness or weakness in the leg, or pain that is worsening instead of settling is worth an assessment before you push through.

slides.headline: Getting dressed shouldn't hurt
slides.body: Our chiropractors assess how your back and hips move, then combine hands-on care with simple exercises. Book online via the link in bio.

caption:
Is putting on your socks and shoes the hardest part of your morning?

Bending, balancing and reaching at the same time can be tough on an irritable back. It's a really common complaint, and it usually says more about sensitivity than damage.

A few things can help: sit down to dress, bring your foot up onto the opposite knee, and use a long-handled shoehorn or slip-ons on flare-up days. Gentle hip hinges and seated bends, done little and often, help the movement come back.

story.body: Sit down, bring your foot onto the opposite knee, and keep a long shoehorn by the door.
